task.description: Implement REQ-073: five real handlers (POST /users, GET /users, GET /users/:id, PATCH /users/:id, POST /users/:id/status) mounted into lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex, per the validated design doc.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: five end-to-end tests (create 201, list cursor page, get 200, patch updated, status-update persisted)
AC2/INV-5: cross-tenant 404 byte-identical to a never-existed 404
AC4: authorization checked before any Repo call in every handler; 403 leaves the database unchanged
AC5/INV-2: response allowlist excludes password_hash/external_id/external_realm, hand-built not derived
AC6: Letflow.Routers.Identity's @moduledoc names each route's Letflow.Identity function(s) verbatim

result.summary:
Implemented all five handlers and their backing Letflow.Identity functions per the design, plus the one additive Authorization clause. Files touched: lib/letflow/identity/user.ex (added create_changeset/2, profile_changeset/2, status_changeset/2), lib/letflow/identity.ex (added create_user/2, list_users/2, get_user/2, update_user_profile/3, update_user_status/3, plus private cursor-pagination helpers), lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex (one additive clause: endpoint_policy_key("POST", "/users/:id/status") -> :UsersManage), lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex (full rewrite of the REQ-070 stub: five routes, shared scoped-prefix+authorization preamble per handler before any Repo call, per-handler Letflow.Api.Validation schemas, hand-built user_map/1 allowlist, AC6 moduledoc), test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs (new, 23 tests).

OQ-3 (password_hash placeholder): chose "__NO_PASSWORD_SET__", mirroring jit_changeset/2's existing "__OIDC_ONLY__" sentinel exactly as the design suggested.

OQ-5 (status_changeset vs. reusing profile_changeset): gave update_user_status/3 its own User.status_changeset/2 with validate_required([:status]), since this changeset's one caller always supplies a validated status and a distinct function documents that contract explicitly rather than relying on profile_changeset/2's all-optional shape.

OQ-2 (timestamp JSON shape): grepped for precedent per the design's instruction -- found lib/letflow/definitions/export_import.ex:97 and lib/letflow/engine/execution_error.ex:231 both using DateTime.to_iso8601/1 for a response-body timestamp. Used the same convention (NaiveDateTime -> DateTime.from_naive!("Etc/UTC") -> to_iso8601/1), noted in the router's own code comment.

Deviation from the design worth flagging explicitly (OQ-1's cursor shape): the design's literal walkthrough (Sec 2.2/Sec 7 gap 2) suggested Pagination.decode_cursor(cursor, "U:", 0) and using a row's own inserted_at as both the sort key and the cursor's freshness-check timestamp. Implementing that literally would make decode_cursor/4's 24h expiry check compare 'now' against the target ROW's inserted_at rather than against when the cursor was minted -- a user created more than 24h ago would make any cursor built from their row appear already-expired the instant it's issued, which contradicts what cursor expiry is supposed to mean (confirmed by reading Letflow.Api.Pagination's own moduledoc/lib/letflow/design/api-pagination.md Sec 5.1: the expiry field is meant to be a mint-time marker). Implemented instead: the cursor payload's first field (checked by decode_cursor's expiry_ts_offset = byte_size("U:") = 2) carries System.system_time(:microsecond) captured at build_next_cursor/1 time; the row's actual inserted_at and id (the real sort key and tiebreaker) are carried in the payload's second/third fields, parsed out in Letflow.Identity's own decode_users_cursor/1 (not by Pagination's generic helpers, which don't interpret cursor contents themselves per that module's own design). This is a field-slot repurposing over Pagination.build_raw_cursor_timestamp_key/4's literal parameter names, not a change to Pagination itself -- documented in-line in lib/letflow/identity.ex's decode_users_cursor/1 comment. Flagging for REVIEWER since it diverges from the design doc's literal offset value (0 vs. 2) and field semantics; I believe the design's own text has a latent bug here (offset 0 would try to parse the "U:" prefix bytes themselves as digits) rather than this being a case where I should have followed it as written.

Test results (real, run to completion this turn): mix compile --warnings-as-errors -- 0 errors, 0 warnings. mix format --check-formatted -- clean after running mix format once (only whitespace/line-wrap changes). test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs: 23/23 passed. Combined with test/letflow/identity_test.exs, test/letflow/router_test.exs, test/letflow/identity/user_test.exs: 78/78 passed. Full project suite (mix test): 1482 passed (5 properties, 1477 tests), 0 failures, 363.9s.

No change to lib/letflow/api/context.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/*.ex, or any other already-done requirement's module beyond the one additive Authorization clause the design named explicitly. No touch to process_instance.ex/InstanceSupervisor -- no state-diagram update needed.
issues: Design doc lib/letflow/design/req073-identity-user-routes.md Sec 2.2/Sec 7 gap 2 (OQ-1) has a likely error in its literal decode_cursor(cursor, "U:", 0) offset and in using a row's own inserted_at as the cursor's freshness-check timestamp -- see summary above for the corrected implementation actually shipped. Not filed as a separate ISS since it's caught and resolved within this same implementation step; flagged here for REVIEWER/TEST-DESIGNER awareness rather than silently diverging.
